name: Shabana Mahmood
role: UK Home Secretary (2025–present); Labour MP for Birmingham Ladywood since 2010; former Justice Secretary and Lord Chancellor
summary: Mahmood is a Labour politician from the party's Blue Labour wing who calls herself a small-c social conservative and a patriot in Orwell's mould. She combines economic positions close to mainstream Labour with strict immigration and asylum controls, expanded policing and surveillance technology, opposition to assisted dying and a gender-critical view of sex. She has long supported Palestinian statehood and the two-state solution.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted for Labour's opposition motions defending the NHS (2016, 2018, 2023) and Corbyn's NHS amendment to the Queen's Speech (2019).

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: As shadow Treasury minister she argued for restoring the 50p top rate, a tax on homes worth over £2m and a bankers' bonus tax, calling the top-rate cut a mistake (2014-15).

cut-welfare.rationale: Opposed the bedroom tax and voted to pause Universal Credit rollout, but as a minister voted against an opposition motion on reversing the winter fuel payment cut (2025).

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voted against the 2023 regulations setting minimum service levels during strikes (rail, border security).

job-guarantee.rationale: In 2013 she backed a compulsory jobs guarantee for every unemployed person under 25, funded by a bank bonus tax; the proposal covers only young people.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: As shadow Treasury minister she spoke of getting the deficit down 'in a fairer way' and 'effective deficit reduction', while criticising the pace of the Government's consolidation; later said she strongly disagreed with Corbyn on economics.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Said settled status gives access to welfare and proposed 'not taking a penny in benefits' as a test for settlement and ending the duty to support asylum seekers; she did not say benefits should be citizens-only.

surveillance-ok.rationale: As Home Secretary she is expanding live facial recognition to all forces and said she wants 'the eyes of the state' on people at all times, 'there is no true liberty if you are unsafe'; the stated aim is crime generally, including terrorism.

empower-police-military.rationale: Pledged 13,000 extra neighbourhood officers, backs wider police use of facial recognition and anonymity for firearms officers charged by the CPS.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Told the Commons she wants 'hate speech and hate crimes always prosecuted' and is reviewing hate crime thresholds, while saying offensive but lawful speech must stay lawful.

rehabilitation.rationale: As Justice Secretary she stressed both rehabilitation and punishment, wanting punishment outside prison expanded and longer sentences possible for some, while cutting overcrowding to allow rehabilitation work.

assisted-dying.rationale: Voted against the assisted dying bills (2015 and 2024-26) and wrote that 'the state should never offer death as a service', citing her Muslim faith and scandals such as Post Office Horizon.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Voted against the 2022 Northern Ireland Troubles (Legacy and Reconciliation) Bill third reading and for amendments to it; later voted for the Labour Government's replacement bill.

religious-exemptions.rationale: In 2015 defended religious non-stun slaughter, saying she does not accept it is cruel if done per Jewish or Islamic texts, and opposed bans.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Told the Commons in 2025: 'We do not have a blasphemy law, and we are not going to have a blasphemy law in this country.'

traditional-family.rationale: Described herself as a small-c social conservative with a natural affinity for the 'faith, family and flag' element of Blue Labour; no specific policy statement found.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted for the Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted for the Abortion (Northern Ireland) Regulations 2021.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: In 2024 she said biological sex 'is real and is immutable' and that she agrees with J. K. Rowling on this.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Called criticism of the 2025 For Women Scotland ruling (sex in the Equality Act means biological sex) 'absolutely unacceptable' and defended gender-critical employees.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Told the Commons in 2019 that RSE should be taught in schools, inclusive of the LGBT community, at the right age and in the right way.

reduce-immigration.rationale: As Home Secretary she is cutting net migration (reporting a fall of nearly 70%) and says 'migration levels are manageable' is a goal, with an end to uncontrolled migration.

open-borders.rationale: Said 'we can only be open to the world if we are able to determine who comes in and who must leave'.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Told the Commons in 2025 'I will never believe in assimilating communities', favouring integration in which communities retain their distinction within a pluralistic whole.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Her settlement rules require higher English (A-level standard for those on visas) as a condition for settling.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Moving settlement from 5 to 10 years as a norm and to 20 years for refugees.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said the pace and scale of migration 'destabilised communities', but also said cohesion has been achieved through diverse communities integrating.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rejected ethno-nationalism, saying it struggles to accept that 'someone who looks like me' can be English or British.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Argued a patriotism that embraces those who 'have a faith like mine' as English or British and warned against ethno-nationalism that denies it.

recognise-genocide.rationale: In 2020-21 said the Chinese government is perpetrating genocide against the Uyghurs and backed a mechanism for courts to determine genocide before trade deals.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Calls for a sovereign Palestine 'alongside a safe and secure Israel'; she did not address a right of the Jewish people to a state directly.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: In 2021 said the occupation and proposed annexation of the West Bank violate international law, and that the occupation must end.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Said any road to peace requires ending the occupation and backed a viable two-state solution including Palestinian statehood.

national-self-determination.rationale: Described Palestinian freedom and statehood as a just cause she has supported her whole life and asked the UK to recognise the state of Palestine (2021).

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Voted against leaving the EU on the Government's terms (Withdrawal Agreement Bill 2019-20) and for amendments softening Brexit, as Labour whips directed.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Voted in 2016 to renew the UK's nuclear deterrent.

close-ties-china.rationale: Said in 2020 it was time for a 'more realistic and clear-eyed approach' to China, calling for a review and reset of the relationship and Magnitsky sanctions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Says Britain will remain in the ECHR and 'will always be' a signatory, while legislating to narrow Article 8 in immigration cases.

nation-first.rationale: Calls her patriotism internationalist in outlook, while her asylum and settlement reforms put border control first.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Describes an Orwellian patriotism and says 'the dice are loaded against working-class communities'; Blue Labour member.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Said 'rights flow from our responsibilities to one another' and 'rights earned through responsibilities fulfilled'.

notes: Frontbench speeches (2010-15 Treasury and education briefs) and votes as a minister follow party and Government lines, so those answers are held at medium or low. She resigned from Corbyn's shadow Treasury team over economics,; the most recent clear statements are used. Her Spectator interview with Michael Gove and Times interviews were not opened.
